name: profile_collapse_relative_minimal_assembly
invariant: Coarser collapse rules cannot increase minimal collapse-relative assembly cost (COMPLEXITY.md section 4's proposition, section 14 item 5), witnessed here as a strict inequality: A_min^fine(x) = 4 > A_min^coarse(x) = 3 for the target observation x = '1 and 3 in the same class'.
explanation: Two candidate histories both attempt to relate object 1 to object 3 via an intermediate object 2, then withdraw the (1,2) relation. candidate_coarse (length 3) achieves '1~3' under the coarse rule (which ignores refusals entirely and unions every bind regardless), but NOT under the fine rule (which honors the withdrawal and so never unions 1 with 2, leaving 1 isolated). candidate_fine (length 4) adds one more bind(1,3) directly, which is enough to achieve '1~3' under both rules. Because 'fine' is strictly the finer rule (it preserves the withdrawal-distinction 'coarse' discards), it can only be satisfied by the longer candidate, giving a strictly larger Collapse-relative minimum -- exactly the direction COMPLEXITY.md section 4's proposition predicts, now with a witness that is strict rather than merely non-strict.
